sources.entry: Twinny - Privacy-first AI extension for local models. #free

summary.one_liner: twinny is a privacy-first AI coding assistant extension for Visual Studio Code that offers code completion, inline edits, chat, and code review using a model server the user chooses, local or hosted.
summary.what_it_does: Provides fill-in-the-middle code completion shown as ghost text, inline edits reviewed as per-hunk diffs (Ctrl+I), and a sidebar chat that can attach files, symbols, problems, git diff, terminal, or workspace search via @ mentions. It includes an experimental agent mode where the model can read, search, and edit files and run commands, with commands asking first by default. A hybrid keyword and vector workspace index is reranked and updated on save, and code review covers the working tree, branches, or GitHub pull requests, plus commit message generation from staged diffs. A terminal feature writes commands from descriptions and can suggest fixes for failed commands. An optional team gateway (twinny-server) serves chat, completion and embeddings to multiple developers with per-person keys and usage tracking; several gateway features require a paid licence.
use_cases: local AI code completion in VS Code
chat with my codebase using a local model
inline code edits with diff review
AI code review of a git branch or pull request
share one model server across a development team
generate commit messages from staged changes
use a hosted API like OpenAI or Anthropic inside VS Code
how_to_run: Install twinny from the Visual Studio Code Marketplace (VS Code 1.93 or newer)
Run a model server such as Ollama, LM Studio, or llama.cpp
Start typing to get completions; use the sidebar for chat
For a team gateway: npx twinny-server quickstart
notable: Works with local servers (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, and others) or hosted APIs, and lets you mix them per task
No telemetry and no sign-in; prompts go only to the server you configure
Team gateway (twinny-server) with per-developer keys, usage tracking, and a hash-chained audit log
Devices feature pairs another computer's GPU over an encrypted peer-to-peer link without an account or relay
Agent mode lets the model edit files and run commands, shown step by step in the reply
caveats: Team gateway features such as policy, recording, plugins and SSO require a paid licence ($15 per seat per month after five free developers, per the README)
Requires a model server to be running or a hosted API key; the README notes a 7B model is the tuning target for completion
keywords: run ai models on my own machine
